correctness.rationale: The root-count pgf is det(qzI+L)/det(qI+L), so R_q is a sum of Bernoulli variables in distribution, with parameters t_j=q/(q+λ_j). The orthogonal Gaussian moments give V_G=2Σt_j². Connectedness gives t_1=1 and contributes −2 to the forest excess; every remaining summand t_j−3t_j² equals 1/12−3(t_j−1/6)². The bound and certificate follow, and equality forces λ_j=5q for all j≥2. The Laplacian is then exactly 5q times the orthogonal projector away from the constant vector, which gives the unique uniform complete conductance matrix and realizes all equality conditions simultaneously. At n=26 the variances are 125/36 and 122/36; the numerator of the complete-graph difference at general n is −2x²+(n−5)x−2n, with discriminant (n−1)(n−25) and positive roots for n≥26. The strict excess persists on an open neighborhood of the complete graph in the positive conductance and q parameters.
residual_risks: The graph statement uses the usual conductance-matrix convention; if parallel edges are allowed the uniqueness is of aggregate conductances, not their splitting. Comparison is for unmodified one-draw variances, not time or cost.

value.rationale: A sharp one-draw variance boundary is a natural benchmark, but this particular certificate and cutoff are a scalar square completion and an elementary equality realization from the already published comparison. The complete-graph window adds only the roots of that same quadratic. There is no independently nonmechanical invariant here, nor does the result resolve computational efficiency, correlated probes, or general-graph crossover sets.
residual_risks: This judgment concerns the frozen raw-variance claim, not the potential value of a different estimator or a cost-aware comparison.
